sanskrit: saṃ vaḥ sṛjatv aryamā saṃ pūṣā saṃ bṛhaspatiḥ | sam indro yo dhanaṃjaya iha puṣyata yad vasu ||
english: May Aryamā unite you together, may Pūṣan unite you, may Bṛhaspati unite you; may Indra, the winner of wealth, unite you — flourish here, whatever wealth there is.

sanskrit: ihaiva gāva etana- -iho śakā iva puṣyata | ihaivota pra jāyadhvaṃ mayi saṃjñānam astu vaḥ ||
english: Come here, O cows, come right here; thrive here like mushrooms growing where they stand. Multiply right here; let there be concord with me among you.

sanskrit: mayā gāvo gopatyā sacadhvam ayaṃ vo goṣṭha iha poṣayāti | rāyaspoṣeṇa bahulā bhavantīr jīvā jīvantīr upa vaḥ sadema ||
english: Stay together with me, your herdsman; this cattle-pen of yours shall nourish you here. Becoming plentiful through the abundance of wealth, alive and thriving, may we sit down beside you.

sanskrit: saṃ vo goṣṭhena suṣadā saṃ rayyā saṃ supuṣṭyā | aharjātasya yan nāma tena vaḥ saṃ sṛjāmasi ||
english: We unite you with your well-seated cattle-pen, with riches, with excellent nourishment. By the name of the one born this day we unite you together.

sanskrit: saṃjānānā avihrutā asmin goṣṭhe karīṣiṇīḥ | bibhratīḥ somyaṃ haviḥ svāveśāsa etana ||
english: In mutual understanding, undispersed, laden with dung-fuel in this cattle-pen, bearing the oblation dear to Soma — enter, each into your own stall.

sanskrit: udyann ādityaḥ krimīn hantu sūryo nimrocan raśmibhir hantu | ye antaḥ krimayo gavi ||
english: As the Āditya rises, may he slay the worms; as the sun sets, may he slay with his rays the worms that are within the cow.

sanskrit: yo viśvarūpaś caturakṣaḥ krimiḥ sāraṅgo arjunaḥ | hato hatabhrātā krimir hatamātā hatasvasā ||
english: The worm that is all-formed, four-eyed, the spotted one, the white one — slain is that worm, slain-brothered, slain-mothered, slain-sistered.

sanskrit: hato rājā krimīṇām utaiṣāṃ sthapatir hataḥ | hatāso asya veśaso hatāsaḥ pariveśasaḥ ||
english: Slain is the king of the worms, and slain is their chief; slain are his neighbours, slain are his neighbours round about.

sanskrit: pra te śṛṇāmi śṛṅge yābhyāṃ tvaṃ vitudāyasi | atho bhinadmi taṃ kumbhaṃ yasmin te nihitaṃ viṣam ||
english: I break off your two horns with which you gore; I also shatter that vessel in which your poison has been placed.

sanskrit: atrivat tvā krime hanmi kaṇvavaj jamadagnivat | agastyasya brahmaṇā sarve te krimayo hatāḥ ||
english: As Atri did, I smite you, O worm; as Kaṇva did, as Jamadagni did. By the sacred formulation of Agastya all your worms are slain.

sanskrit: indrasya yā mahī dṛṣat krimer viśvasya tarhaṇī | tayā pinaṣmi saṃ krimīn dṛṣadā khalvām̐ iva ||
english: That great grinding-stone of Indra, crusher of every worm — with it I grind up the worms with the millstone, as grain in a hand-mill.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭam adṛṣṭam atṛham atho kurūrum atṛham | algaṇḍūn sarvāñ chalūlān krimīn vacasā jambhayāmasi ||
english: The seen and the unseen I have crushed; I have also crushed the kurūru. The algaṇḍu-worms, all the śalūla-worms — with the sacred word we crush the worms.

sanskrit: algaṇḍūn hanmi mahatā vadhena dūnā adūnā arasā abhūvan | śiṣṭān aśiṣṭān ni tirāmi vācā yathā krimīṇāṃ nakir ucchiṣātai ||
english: I smite the algaṇḍu-worms with a great blow; the afflicted and the unafflicted have become devoid of essence. Those remaining and those not yet reached I overwhelm with the sacred word, so that not one of the worms shall survive.

sanskrit: anvāntriyaṃ śīrṣaṇyam atho pārṣṭeyaṃ krimim | avaskavaṃ vyadvaraṃ krimīn vacasā jambhayāmasi ||
english: The intestinal worm, the head worm, and the worm of the ribs, the avaskava, the vyadhvara — with the sacred word we crush the worms.

sanskrit: ye krimayaḥ parvateṣu ye vaneṣu ya oṣadhīṣu paśuṣv apsv antaḥ | ye asmākaṃ tanvaṃ sthāma cakrira indras tān hantu mahatā vadhena ||
english: The worms that are in the mountains, those that are in the forests, those in the plants, within cattle, within the waters — those that have made our body their abode, may Indra smite them with a great blow.
